We welcome you to the Youth Commission meeting.

If you wish to address the Commission during the meeting, please complete a speaker’s card and
give it to the secretary. The maximum time for addressing the Commission is five minutes. If
you wish to address the Commission on an item which appears on the agenda, your comments will
be heard during the Commission’s discussion of that item. If you wish to address the Commission
on a subject which does not appear on the agenda but related to recreation or community service,
you may make your presentation under agenda item VII. Please be advised that the Commission
cannot, under the State of California’s Ralph M. Brown Act, take action on any item which does
not appear on the agenda.

When making your presentation, please give your name and address for the record. Please make
your statement as brief as possible. Thank you.

minutes_text:
APPROVED by: Youth Commission on November 12th, 2019

  MINUTES
  Alhambra Youth Commission
  August 13, 2019

The Alhambra Youth Commission was called to order at 6:00 pm on August 13, 2019 at the
Alhambra Public Library Conference Room, 101 S. First Street, Alhambra, CA.

Commission Members Present: Esmerio, Guzman, Jimenez, Lou, Martinez, Placido, and
Webster

Commission Members Absent: Duong, Garcia, Gonzalez, Gutierrez, Luc, Olmeda, Romero,
and Yan

Also present: Vincent Hon, Recreation Supervisor.

III.  APPROVAL OF THE JUNE 11, 2019 YOUTH COMMISSION MEETING
  MINUTES

  On the motion from Commissioner Martinez and second by Commissioner Webster
  the Minutes of June 11, 2019 were approved.

IV.  DISCUSSION REGARDING THE 4TH OF JULY CELEBRATION
  VOLUNTEER OPPORTUNITY

  Recreation Supervisor Hon discusses the 4th of July event and asks the
  Commissioners to describe their experiences volunteering for the event. He asks
  Commissioner Placido how her interactions with the public participating in the
  event went. Commissioner Placido stated that she worked the carnival games and it
  was a lot of fun. Mr. Hon then proceed to talk about the 2nd annual 4th of July hot
  dog eating contest. Mr. Hon stated that there was a total of 12 contestants and that
  the winner ate a total of 9 hotdogs and won a $100 gift card to Target as a grand
  prize.

  Mr. Hon then asked the Commissioners what they thought about the inflatable
  garden located on field three. The commissioners that were in attendance thought it
  was a cool element. Mr. Hon later explains that “jumpers” are no longer allowed
  during major city events due to the possibility of lawsuits as per direction by the
  human resources department. Recreation Supervisor Hon opens up the floor for
  any suggestions on what can replace the “jumper” section of upcoming special
  events. Commissioner Placido and Jimenez suggested a maze or relay race for an
  option that could replace the “jumper” section. Mr. Hon discusses the budget
  allotted to special events and that he only gets a certain amount that he can spend
  on these events so it will be challenging to see what will replace the inflatables
  based on the budget.

  Mr. Hon gives more details about the 4th of July event and asks for the
  Commissioners’ opinion on the fireworks show and explains that the firework
  show was cut short due to a malfunction in the firework system. The
  Commissioners commented that the show was good but didn’t enjoy that there
  wasn’t a “grand finale”. Recreation Supervisor Hon explains that he will make sure
   the next 4th of July event is more organized and that the duties of the
  Commissioners will be outlined more precisely.

V.  DISCUSSION REGARDING LATINO HERITAGE FESTIVAL AND
  FUTURE EVENTS

  Recreation Supervisor Hon describes the next upcoming event which will be the
  Latino Heritage Festival. It will be an extension of the farmer’s market that occurs
  every Sunday and there will be vendors selling various foods and items related to
  the Latin culture. There will also be face painting stations and craft booths oriented
  for children. Mr. Hon said there will be various performances as well during the
  event. Mr. Hon goes on to ask who can volunteer for the event and outlines what
  will needed to be done for the event. The volunteers will assist with the craft
  booths in addition to decorating the stage and tent that covers the dance floor. Mr.
  stated that he will send an email to the Commissioners to confirm who will
  volunteer for this event.

  Mr. Hon then outlines another event, the “Pumpkin Run”, that will be occurring in
  October and provide another opportunity for the Commissioners to volunteer. Mr.
  Hon stated that he will provide more information at the next meeting.

  Lastly, Recreation Supervisor Hon outlines the “Tech Talk” volunteer opportunity
  that runs from its new times of 3:30 pm to 4:30 pm., every first Thursday of the
  month at the Joslyn Center. This is an opportunity where a Commissioner can
  assist someone with their technologic needs consisting of assistance with both
  electronics and social media, etc. The next “Tech Talk” will be the first Thursday
  in September which falls on the 5th of September. Mr. Hon stated that he will send
  an email to the Commissioners to see who can volunteer.

VI.  ORAL COMMUNICATIONS

  There are no oral communications at this time.

VII.  COMMISSION ORALS

  No Commissioners had additional comments.

VIII. ADJOURNMENT

  The meeting was adjourned at 6:40 p.m. by Recreation Supervisor Vincent Hon.
